transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-11-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Desai, Lina Gomez, Marcus Chen (Redwood); Dr Elaine Park, Naveen Rao, Sofia Alvarez (Pinecrest)

Summary:
Quick triage around long tail queue accumulation observed last Friday during the 14:30-15:10 window. Focus on identifying root cause candidates: client retries and pacing, KV cache pressure, quantization CPU stalls, and burst scheduling on shared hosted pool. Action plan agreed for replay tests, evidence collection and short Dedicated sandbox.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and impact
- Candidate causes and evidence gaps
- Replay/test plan and environment needs
- Security and contractual asks for pilot
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00:03] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining i know this is a follow up after last weeks spike. we tried to keep this tight, 45 minutes ish, and then we can extend if need be. do you want to start with the quick impact summary Elaine?
[00:00:17] Dr Elaine Park: yeah thanks Samir. we saw a sustained ramp in queued requests hitting redwood api starting around 14 31 local. our front end started to throt, pages were slow, some urgent patients searches timed out for a few minutes. overall about 6 of our support tickets were escalated.
[00:00:31] Naveen: to add, the majority of these were 1 to 2 token generation calls from triage microservices, but the tail latency really spiked p99s went from 400ms to 4.2s for a ~20 minute window.
[00:00:45] Samir: ok that aligns with our logs, we saw backlog growth on the shared pool for the hosted plan. Lina can you confirm what Redwood saw on the runtime side?
[00:00:53] Lina: briefly yeah so from our side we saw increased queue depth at the ingress for that tenant id. CPU on the host nodes showed intermittent user time spikes and some context switches that lined up with the KV cache GC cycles, though i want to be careful, the mapping isnt 1 to 1. also notice a few frequent client retry bursts that looked like exponential backoff misconfiguration.
[00:01:13] Sofia: we did have retries from our platform yeah, we rolled out a new retry wrapper on the client last week, and we had a lower initial backoff which may have caused tight replays under transient error. i can share that patch.
[00:01:24] Marcus: so two things then client behavior plus runtime KV pressure. do you think quantization could have contributed? i remember Lina mentioned some kernel context switching around quantized models.
[00:01:34] Lina: possible. when models are running in q4_0 or int8 paths we sometimes see CPU fallback for certain ops when kernel vectorization isnt optimal on a host, that spikes latency for specific sequence lengths. again its hypothesis. we should reproduce with quantization toggled.
[00:01:49] Dr Elaine Park: timeline wise we need an answer quickly. our compliance team flagged the incident and legal wants to know if we hit any data exposure, and our product ops folks want mitigation plan.
[00:02:01] Samir: understood. on data exposure we saw no anomalies in audit logs, no payload leakage. but Marcus will follow up with the audit evidence and a summary for legal.
[00:02:10] Marcus: yes im on it, i will export the request traces and the access log subset and drop in the secure share.
[00:02:19] [00:02:20] Naveen: one other note we saw host scaling attempts fail a couple of times, autoscaler didnt add nodes quickly enough. maybe queueing backed up while scaler converged.
[00:02:30] Lina: that matches an observed interplay between our continuous batching engine and the autoscaler weve been tuning. when batch sizes and concurrency bump there is a transient where batches get held waiting for next token loop, which can exacerbate queue length.
[00:02:45] Samir: so immediate hypothesis list: client retry storms, KV cache GC pressure, quantization fallbacks causing CPU stalls, autoscaler convergence lag. we should prioritize reproducibility tests.
[00:02:56] Dr Elaine Park: what are the recommended immediate mitigations we can apply from Pinecrest side? we cant flip your runtime settings but we can change client behavior and maybe throttle certain endpoints.
[00:03:07] Sofia: we can patch client backoff immediately and push a hotfix to increase initial backoff to 200ms and cap retries. we should do that now.
[00:03:15] Samir: good immediate step. also on Redwood side we can temporarily enable stricter per-tenant concurrency caps for your org to keep queue length bounded while we run tests. that requires a short outage window to flip, but we can schedule.
[00:03:27] Naveen: ok, do that. also for the longer term we want guardrails so these dont recur in production.
[00:03:32] Lina: proposal for repro: we want the exact request traces for the 14 30 window, full headers and timing, and a reproducible replay harness at your side or ours. we can run three variants: baseline (current), kv cache disabled, quantization disabled. compare p50 p95 p99 and CPU profile.
[00:03:48] Dr Elaine Park: we can provide traces but need assurance on data handling. we cant send PHI to external parties unless encrypted in transit and stored in your pilot sandbox. legal will require an MOU.
[00:03:59] Samir: absolutely, Marcus will attach the MOU template and we will use a short-lived sandbox with customer managed keys. we can provide a Dedicated trial with VPC peering if that helps.
[00:04:10] Marcus: note on that, our Dedicated sandbox will have isolation and we can offer HSM or KMS integration for keys. legal usually accepts that level of control.
[00:04:18] Sofia: that sounds good. timeline?
[00:04:21] Samir: we proposed a two week sandbox, quick replay runs in the first week and then a tuning week. Lina can run the replays once we have traces and the sandbox.
[00:04:29] Lina: yes also request you include the client version and the retry wrapper details. small differences in request pacing change batching characteristics.
[00:04:36] Naveen: i will extract traces and scrub PHI fields, but we want to keep request shape intact. we will use Pinecrest managed encryption key and share via the secure transfer link.
[00:04:45] Dr Elaine Park: ok. one more question around alerting: why didnt our alerting pick this up earlier? our infra pages saw increased error counts but maybe thresholding is off.
[00:04:55] Samir: good question. for hosted customers we can push fine grained request queue alerts to your pager but they need to be enabled per tenant; Marcus will help enable and tune thresholds.
[00:05:05] Marcus: agreed, ill open a ticket to configure queue depth alerts and a short runbook for triage.
[00:05:11] [00:05:12] Sofia: can we have a rollback plan if the sandbox changes cause regressions?
[00:05:16] Lina: sandbox changes are isolated, but for live config we recommend feature flags and canaries. also we can configure auto fallback to a smaller model instance if p99 breaches.
[00:05:25] Dr Elaine Park: okay action items and who's doing what, maybe read them back.
[00:05:29] Samir: sure. readback 1, Pinecrest to patch client backoff today, Sofia and Naveen. 2, Pinecrest to provide scrubbed request traces and retry wrapper by 2025-11-07. 3, Redwood to provide MOU and sandbox provisioning steps by 2025-11-06. 4, Lina to run quantified replays comparing kv cache and quantization toggles by 2025-11-09. 5, Marcus to export audit logs and share legal summary by 2025-11-10. 6, Marcus to enable tenant queue alerts and create runbook by 2025-11-08.
[00:06:07] Dr Elaine Park: that sounds good. one last note our product lead wants an estimate on timeline to complete stabilizations so they can communicate to stakeholders. can you provide a rough recovery cadence?
[00:06:19] Samir: rough cadence is fast mitigation under 48 hours for obvious fixes like client backoff and tenant caps. repro and tuning 1 to 2 weeks, pilot in Dedicated 2 weeks, longer term runtime hardening 4 to 8 weeks depending on kernel changes. we will provide a milestone plan in the next update.
[00:06:34] Naveen: can you add an explicit handoff session between Redwood infra kernel folks and our SREs? we will need deeper profiling.
[00:06:41] Lina: yes we will schedule a technical deep dive with our runtime team once we have replay artifacts. probably a 90 minute session.
[00:06:48] Samir: ok im going to capture the follow ups and close out. thanks everyone.

End of transcript
